root_cause.text: In the CPSW dual-EMAC driver (`drivers/net/ethernet/ti/cpsw_new.c`), `cpsw_unregister_ports()` only checked whether `slaves[i].ndev` was non-NULL, so an error during `cpsw_register_ports()` could leave a second `net_device` pointer intact even though it was never successfully registered, leading to an invalid `unregister_netdev()` call.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `cpsw_unregister_ports()` from `if (!ndev) continue;` to `if (!ndev || ndev->reg_state != NETREG_REGISTERED) continue;`, and removes the `cpsw->slaves[i].ndev = NULL;` cleanup from the error path in `cpsw_register_ports()`, matching the CVE text that “cpsw->slaves[1].ndev would remain unchanged” and could later cause unregister of the second MAC.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid unregistering CPSW slave ports unless their netdevices are actually registered.
intent_record.what: In cpsw_unregister_ports(), the loop condition was changed from skipping only when ndev is NULL to skipping when ndev is NULL or when ndev->reg_state is not NETREG_REGISTERED.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will no longer attempt to unregister or access network devices that exist but are not in the registered state, preventing operations on partially initialized or already-unregistered netdevices.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the explicit NULL assignment to the slave netdevice pointer in the port registration failure path.
intent_record.what: A single statement was removed from the error path in `cpsw_register_ports()`: the assignment `cpsw->slaves[i].ndev = NULL;` is no longer executed when registering a net device fails.
intent_record.how: On registration failure, the code now breaks out of the loop without explicitly clearing the failed slave's `ndev` pointer. This preserves the existing pointer state instead of forcing it to NULL in that error path.

candidates.rationale: This retrieves the slave net_device pointer and is followed by only a NULL check; because an unsuccessful registration could leave a non-NULL but unregistered pointer in the array, later unregister logic would treat it as valid and call unregister_netdev() on it.

The unregister path only guards on NULL here, which is insufficient for distinguishing a successfully registered net_device from one that was allocated but never registered, directly enabling the invalid unregister.

This explicit clearing of the slave net_device pointer on registration failure prevented later teardown from attempting to unregister an unregistered device; its presence indicates the missing safeguard that caused the bug.

vuln_statements.explanation: This NULL-only guard in cpsw_unregister_ports() allowed the code to treat any non-NULL slave net_device pointer as registered, even if cpsw_register_ports() had failed before registration completed. That directly led to an invalid unregister_netdev() call on an unregistered device.

This fetches the slave net_device pointer that is later checked only for NULL. Because a failed registration could leave a stale non-NULL pointer in the array, this statement participates in the teardown path that incorrectly unregisters an unregistered net_device.
